key_facts: This document sets out rules for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix, which took place from 30 October to 1 November 2026.
The rules cover safety procedures, pit lane entry and exit, track limits, and how drivers must behave during qualifying, practice, and the race.
Drivers must allow faster cars to pass when they are being lapped, signalled by blue light panels when the faster car is within 1.2 seconds.
Drivers who exceed a maximum time between two Safety Car Lines during qualifying or reconnaissance laps may be penalised for going unnecessarily slowly.
Several sections of the circuit have been resurfaced or marked with new lines to clarify track limits and safe routes for rejoining the track.
plain_explanation:
This document gives competition rules for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. It covers many topics that apply to practice, qualifying, and the race.

One rule is about drivers who are caught and lapped by faster cars during the race. The International Sporting Code requires a driver being lapped to let the faster driver past at the first chance. The marshalling system (the trackside control system) will warn the slower driver's team when the faster car is 3 seconds away, and will show blue light panels to the slower car when the faster car is within 1.2 seconds. At that point, the driver being lapped must allow the faster car to overtake at the first available opportunity.

Another rule is about qualifying and reconnaissance laps. Any driver who takes too long to go from the Second Safety Car Line to the First Safety Car Line on any lap during or after qualifying, including in-laps and out-laps, or during reconnaissance laps when pit exit opens for the race, may be treated as going unnecessarily slowly. The teams and drivers are told the maximum time after the second practice session. This rule does not change the regulations that already apply to the whole circuit and the pit lane.

The document also sets detailed rules about pit lane entry and exit, parc fermé (a closed area where cars are controlled after qualifying or the race), practice starts, and how cars must rejoin the track if they go off at certain corners. For Turn 4, if a driver goes off into the run-off area and crosses a yellow line with all four wheels, they must rejoin via a specific asphalt route. For Turn 11, a driver whose car passes completely behind the red and white kerb must rejoin by keeping to the right of the first polystyrene block and then to the left of the second.

For safety car procedures, the document says that waved yellow flags and "SC" boards will not be used. Instead, when the safety car deploys, the message "SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED" will be sent to all teams and a trackside light panel will display "SC". When the safety car lights turn off, the message "SAFETY CAR LIGHTS OFF" will be sent to all teams, and a green light panel will show at the Control Line.

The circuit has been resurfaced from after Turn 11 until before Turn 1. Several new blue lines have been added to mark safe routes, and some kerbs and white lines have been changed to make track limits clearer.
